title: Scheme representations of finitely presented fpqc forms spread along affine limits
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to S$ be flat, surjective and quasi-compact with $A$ affine [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and let $F$ be a contravariant set-valued functor on $S$-schemes satisfying the fpqc covering equalizer condition. Assume $F_A$ is represented by a separated $A$-scheme $P$ of finite presentation [def-pc-representable-functor, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Here separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(T_i)$ be an inverse system of affine $S$-schemes, and let $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$ with its specified projections [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose given a representation $h_Y\simeq F_T$ by a separated $T$-scheme $Y$ of finite presentation. Then there are $i\in I$, a separated $T_i$-scheme $Y_i$ of finite presentation, and a representation $h_{Y_i}\simeq F_{T_i}$ whose base change is the specified representation: there is an isomorphism $Y_i\times_{T_i}T\simeq Y$ making these maps to $F_T$ equal. No flatness or surjectivity is required of $T\to T_i$ or of the transition morphisms.

source.place: Raynaud, Un critere d effectivite de descente, Theorem 4.1 proof, reductions 3 and 4, printed pp.5-19--5-20. Primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $B_i=A\times_ST_i$ and $C_i=A\times_SA\times_ST_i$, and put $B=A\times_ST$ and $C=A\times_SA\times_ST$. All $T_i,B_i,C_i$ are affine, hence qcqs, and every transition is affine. The fibre-product universal property identifies $B=\varprojlim B_i$ and $C=\varprojlim C_i$: a compatible family of maps to $B_i$ is exactly a map to $A$ and a compatible family to $T_i$ over $S$; the same argument uses two maps to $A$ for $C_i$. The affine-limit theorem supplies these scheme limits. Thus all three systems satisfy the base hypotheses of finite-presentation continuity. Write $P_{B_i}=P\times_A B_i$; over $C_i$ distinguish $P_{1,C_i}$ and $P_{2,C_i}$ using its first and second maps to $A$. These schemes are finitely presented over their indicated bases by base-change permanence.

source.place: Tags 01YW, 01YX (affine inverse limits); Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), preparation; Tags 01I4, 01TS for affine products and base change

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of finite-presentation continuity to $Y/T$. Obtain $i_0$, a finitely presented $T_{i_0}$-scheme $V_{i_0}$, and a specified isomorphism $\lambda:V_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T\simeq Y$. For $i\ge i_0$ set $V_i=V_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$. These are finitely presented, and qcqs since the bases are affine and finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The given representations and $\lambda$ induce an isomorphism of representable functors over $B$, hence a scheme isomorphism $\alpha:V_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}B\simeq P\times_AB$. Explicitly, Yoneda sends a natural map to its value at the identity; applying this to the map and its inverse makes their composites identities. Choose the orientation so the representation of $P_B$ composed with $h_\alpha$ equals the specified representation of $Y$ composed with $h_{\lambda_B}$.

Apply clause (2) of finite-presentation continuity over the affine system $(B_i)$ to $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$. Directedness gives one common stage for both arrows. The two composites agree with the respective identities over $B$; clause (3), applied twice and then at a common later stage, makes both inverse equations hold there. We obtain a scheme isomorphism $\alpha_i:V_i\times_{T_i}B_i\simeq P_{B_i}$ whose base change is exactly $\alpha$. All models here are finitely presented over $B_i$, not merely over $T_i$, by step 1 and base change of $V_i$. Thus neither the existence of the arrows nor their inverse equations requires the map $B\to B_i$ to be flat or surjective.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(2),(3) (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), applied to an isomorphism and its inverse

proof.text: Let $\rho:h_P\simeq F_A$ be the chosen local representation. Over $A\times_SA$, its two pullbacks give a natural isomorphism $\rho_2^{-1}\rho_1:h_{P_1}\simeq h_{P_2}$; Yoneda gives the corresponding scheme isomorphism $\delta:P_1\simeq P_2$. Over $C_i$ consider the two arrows from $V_i\times_{T_i}C_i$ to $P_{2,C_i}$: $\delta_{C_i}\circ\alpha_{i,1}$ and $\alpha_{i,2}$. Their base changes to $C$ agree because $\alpha$ was defined using the single representation of $Y/T$; composing with $\rho_2$ makes both maps the restriction of that representation composed with $h_\lambda$. Apply clause (3) of continuity to the system $(C_j)_{j\ge i}$ and these two arrows. Its source and target models are finitely presented over $C_i$ by base change. After enlarging $i$, we therefore have the actual overlap equation $\delta_{C_i}\alpha_{i,1}=\alpha_{i,2}$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(3) (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); Categories Tag 001P; the compatibility equation needed in Raynaud Theorem 4.1 proof, reduction 4

proof.text: Set $Y_i=V_i$. For every $H\to T_i$, the map $H_A=H\times_SA\to H$ is an fpqc cover by base-change stability. The isomorphism $\alpha_i$ and $\rho$ give a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{T_i}(H_A,V_i)\simeq F(H_A)$. Step 4 says that this bijection intertwines the two restriction maps to $H_A\times_HH_A$: indeed $\rho_1=\rho_2h_\delta$ and $\delta\alpha_{i,1}=\alpha_{i,2}$. On one side, scheme fpqc morphism descent identifies the equalizer with $\operatorname{Hom}_{T_i}(H,V_i)$; the descended map is over $T_i$ since its structure-map equality holds on the cover and scheme descent gives uniqueness. On the other side, the assumed fpqc equalizer condition identifies the equalizer with $F(H)$. Consequently we have a bijection $\theta_{i,H}:\operatorname{Hom}_{T_i}(H,V_i)\simeq F(H)$. Its inverse takes an element of $F(H)$, uses $\alpha_i^{-1}$ locally to obtain a compatible map $H_A\to V_i$, and descends that map uniquely. Restrictions commute with both constructions, since they do so on $H_A$ and both descents are unique. Thus $\theta_i:h_{V_i}\simeq F_{T_i}$ is a representation, constructed without assuming that $F_{T_i}$ was already a scheme.

source.place: Tags 022D (topologies-lemma-fpqc) and 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); covering equalizer assumption on F

proof.text: The cover $B_i\to T_i$ is the base change of $A\to S$, so $\{B_i\to T_i\}$ is an fpqc covering by clause (3) of the covering axioms; by the definition of fpqc coverings $B_i\to T_i$ is flat, and it is surjective since its image contains every affine open of $T_i$. It is quasi-compact because $B_i$ is affine, hence quasi-compact, and $T_i$ is affine, hence quasi-separated. Under $\alpha_i$, the base change of $V_i\to T_i$ is $P_{B_i}\to B_i$, which is separated by separated base-change permanence. Fpqc descent of separatedness therefore makes $V_i\to T_i$ separated; finite presentation was preserved throughout steps 2--4. Finally base change of $\theta_i$ to $T$ equals the specified representation of $Y$ composed with $h_\lambda$: their restrictions over $B$ agree by the defining equation for $\alpha$, and for each test scheme their values are equal because the fpqc equalizer map for $F$ is injective. Hence the already specified $\lambda:V_i\times_{T_i}T\simeq Y$ has exactly the compatibility demanded in the statement. All uses of fpqc descent were along base changes of $A\to S$; the transition maps and limit projections needed only to be affine.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01ZM(1)--(3) plus fpqc equalizers (023Q); explicit filling of the analogous limit argument invoked by Raynaud Theorem 4.1 proof, reduction 4, printed p.5-20.
